signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + JPY Underperformance
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 114.40 amid a clear divergence in G10 performance where CAD averages +0.783% against its peers while JPY lags at -0.837%. The leader-to-laggard spread of 1.620% signals a strong bilateral theme, further supported by a 125bp OIS carry advantage for the Canadian dollar. Despite growing BoJ hike expectations and rising JGB yields, JPY remains the weakest G10 performer, failing to attract safe-haven bids even as global manufacturing data improves. Technical positioning for JPY shows USD/JPY at 159.33, holding below its SMA20/50 cluster but above the SMA200 at 158.12, suggesting the JPY-weakness trend remains structurally intact. CAD strength is reinforced by a moderate positive ESI of +12.0, contrasting with the broader USD soft patch. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; carry advantage and G10 divergence favor continued upside. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — hold priced. Risk: Sharp risk-off deleveraging triggers JPY short-covering, compressing the 1.620% spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + Positioning
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.33 exhibits a significant decoupling between spot carry and the options market. While the 265bp SOFR-TONA carry differential supports the long USD stance, the 25d risk reversal at -2.19 reflects a strong put skew, indicating that institutional players are paying a premium for downside protection. This options caution aligns with a crowded COT speculative position, where JPY net shorts total -63,633. The negative -1.5% VRP suggests the options market is currently pricing in less volatility than realized, creating a window for a sharp move if BoJ hike expectations at the 18 Sep meeting continue to build. Price action remains capped below the SMA20/50 cluster at 160.93/161.15. Trade bias: Neutral/Short USD/JPY; strong options downside skew suggests hedging against carry-trade exhaustion. Catalyst: US CPI print 12 Aug. Risk: Benign inflation data weakens the USD, accelerating the JPY short-squeeze toward the SMA200 at 158.12.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + Retail Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3505 is trading above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, indicating a solid technical bull trend. However, the options market is pricing in significant tail risk, with IV at 11.0% vs HV30 at 6.0%, resulting in a 5.0% volatility risk premium—the highest in the G10 space. This elevated hedging demand comes as retail sentiment reaches a 70% short extreme, providing a contrarian signal that supports further institutional upside. Speculative positioning via COT shows a net long of +39,039 (70.1% long), which aligns with the price trend but warns of potential crowding if the 1.3550 resistance holds. The neutral OIS carry differential of -10bp means the pair lacks a clear interest rate driver, making it highly sensitive to the upcoming US inflation data. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD; retail short extreme and positive technical posture support a move toward 1.3600. Catalyst: US CPI print 12 Aug. Risk: US inflation beat triggers broad USD recovery, forcing an unwind of the 70.1% spec long.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Real Rate Divergence + COT Positioning
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7066 continues to find support from a restrictive real policy rate of +0.60%, contrasting with the USD real rate of +1.53% as markets weigh energy-related inflation risks in Australia. COT data reveals an AUD net long of +37,990 with a 72.1% long ratio, showing that speculative conviction is nearing extreme levels. This institutional length is being faded by retail traders, who are currently 76% short, creating a classic divergence that typically favors trend continuation. Technically, the pair is positioned above all major moving averages, with the SMA20 at 0.7013 providing immediate dynamic support. While OIS carry favors the AUD by 72bp, the proximity to the psychological 0.7100 level and crowded positioning is likely to limit immediate follow-through without a fresh macro catalyst. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; supported by real rate differential and contrarian retail signals. Catalyst: US CPI print 12 Aug. Risk: RBA shift toward a cut bias on cooling data invalidates the hawkish AUD narrative.
